question: On 9/28/76, the HUD Secretary (at the time) made a speech to the Ft Worth Federal Business Association; I know the Ford Presidential Library has a copy of the final version of that speech text, though I can't find it at the moment. I want you to find that library's copy of that speech version for me, because there are some lines of poetry quoted in that speech, and I want to use them myself -- can you reply with just the title and author of the poem from which those quoted lines are taken? If the secretary misquoted the poem a bit, that's okay -- I expect that the full quote of the poem will give a very clear understanding of which poem was being referred to. Give your answer in the following form: "[TITLE], by [AUTHOR]". For example, if the poem was The Road Not Taken, written by Robert Frost, you would answer: The Road Not Taken, by Robert Frost

tool_calls.result: The lines> “For all your days prepare,  >  And meet them ever alike:  >  When you are the anvil, bear—  >  When you are the hammer, strike.”  are taken from Edwin Markham’s poem **“Preparedness”** (often referred to as “The Anvil and the Hammer”).  The poem appears in the 1928 collection *The Gates of Paradise and Other Poems* and is in the public domain.You can view the full poem on the Poetry Foundation website:<https://www.poetryfoundation.org/poems/47959/preparedness>Carla A. Hills cited this verse in her September 28, 1976 HUD Secretary speech to the Fort Worth Federal Business Association, using it as a metaphor for the partnership between federal government (“the anvil”) and the private sector (“the hammer”).

The user wants the title and author: "[TITLE], by [AUTHOR]". We should reply "Preparedness, by Edwin Markham". Alternatively mention "The Anvil and the Hammer, by Edwin Markham". The standard title seems "Preparedness". The speech quoting lines: "For all your days prepare. Treat them not alike. When you’re the anvil—bear, When you’re the hammer—strike!" That is likely from "Preparedness". So answer: Preparedness, by Edwin Markham.
